newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland unveils plan to combat drug addiction.
newsitem.headline: Ireland unveils plan to combat drug addiction.

text.p: Ireland's government published plans on Friday to combat what it called the "epidemic" of drug addiction gripping Dublin.

A government report promised a 14-million-punt ($22.5 million) package to tackle the problem, including extra resources to treat addicts and an improvement programme for severely run-down urban areas.

It contained plans for greater co-operation among state agencies fighting the drugs threat, as well as the creation of local drugs task forces in partnership with community groups in areas facing the most acute problem.

"This report is an important step in tackling the drugs problem from the demand side, with its focus on treatment, education, research and the causes of drug addiction," government minister Pat Rabbitte told a news conference.
Community groups say Dublin's drugs problem is one of the worst in Europe. In some areas drugs are traded openly in the streets and addicts can be seen queueing up for a fix.

Ireland has also become a hub of the international drugs trade, customs officials say, as its miles of remote coastline are ideal for smuggling in drugs for trans-shipment to the rest of Europe. Half a tonne of cocaine was seized from a trawler in the southern port of Cork this month.
The government has taken several anti-drugs initiatives since investigative journalist Veronica Guerin was murdered in Dublin in July.
Guerin had exposed the activities of criminal godfathers running Dublin's drugs trade and police believe one of them ordered her murder.
